meta.story: 134.6 (baseline half — measures the build as it stands, before the uplift)
meta.load_caveat: a background process permanently pins a core on this machine, so a 1-min load average below 2 is unreachable; --allow-load was used and every number here is therefore measured on a loaded machine. Medians and p95s are inflated relative to an idle box; treat them as an upper bound on latency and a lower bound on throughput.

meta.knee_recomputed: knee() was corrected after the run (degrades_at was reporting c=1, the lowest level below peak, rather than the first level ABOVE peak that fell 5 % below it); the correction is a pure re-read of the same `levels` arrays, which are untouched

cold_start_ms.definition: wall from just before fork/exec to the first byte of the first HTTP 200 on /api/health; the client busy-polls connect() so poll granularity is ~0.2 ms, not a fixed sleep

rss_kb_idle.note: sum of RSS over the server's whole process group (`ps -o rss= -g <pgid>`), sampled 1 s after the first 200 and before any load; includes forked workers, so copy-on-write pages are counted once per worker — the per-pid breakdown is given so the sum can be discounted

rate_limit.method: sequential fresh TCP connections, one request each, closed by the client

static.definition: fresh: connect() through to the first byte of the response, one new TCP connection per sample, connection setup INCLUDED — what a browser sees on a cold link. reused: send through first byte on an already-open keep-alive connection — the server's own service time.

static.mode: keep-alive, one connection per client thread, reconnect on close, server restarted before each concurrency level
static.client: python3 threads, blocking sockets. Control: at c=1 the measured requests/second equals 1/mean-latency to three digits, so the client adds no measurable per-request overhead at that level. Above ~8 threads the GIL is a plausible ceiling; the caddy rows are the control — where caddy goes higher on the same route, the client was not the limit.

knee.rule: peak = highest rps in the sweep; degrades_at = lowest concurrency above the peak whose rps is more than 5 % below it; null = no such level inside the sweep

ooke.label: ooke-toke `serve` on ooke's own testproj scaffold
ooke.stack: ooke src/serve.tk -> toke std.http. NOTE: ooke renders every page ONCE at startup (serveregisterstatic -> http.getstatic) and serves the rendered HTML from memory, so its page route is an in-memory static response, NOT a per-request render. The website binary's http.servepages re-reads and re-renders the .tkt from disk on every request. The two 'page' numbers are therefore different workloads and must not be compared head to head.
